title: Damac and Hussain Sajwani: fees for unannounced projects and the data-centre pledge
summary: The money and the relationship are well documented. Damac paid about $10M in 2025 to two new Trump licensing entities that CREW says appear tied to unannounced Abu Dhabi developments, with no launched project by Nov 2026. Sajwani's ties to Trump run from the 2013 golf deal through Mar-a-Lago, an April 2025 Oval Office visit and the May 2025 Abu Dhabi forum. The $20B pledge has become about $12B of land and power: a $36.5M site in Canton, Ohio, a New Jersey site and an $860M Kansas conversion, none of them operating. Every approval found is local. No federal permit, FAST-41 designation or energy decision for a Damac site was found, and no Sajwani link to WLF, USD1 or $TRUMP turned up.

sub_claims.statement: Damac paid about $10M in 2025 for two Abu Dhabi Trump licences, and as of Nov 2026 no Trump-branded Abu Dhabi project has been launched.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (Trump's 2026 OGE disclosure as read by CREW, CNBC and The National). This repeats C70/C82 only to bring it up to date. Two Damac subsidiaries paid $5M each to DT Marks Abu Dhabi LLC and DT Marks Al Raha Beach LLC. The National ties the money to 'an estate project at Abu Dhabi's Al Raha Beach'. CNBC (10 Aug 2026) says the Trump Organization has no active development there and puts Damac's 2025 total at $11.3M, against about $12.5M from CREW and The National. New since C82: searches through Nov 2026 found no Damac or Trump Organization launch in Abu Dhabi. One property-portal analysis expects a Damac Abu Dhabi villa community in 2026 but names no site and no Trump brand. Forbes (Oct 2025) estimated that Damac companies pay Trump about $6M a year on the older Dubai golf deals. CREW (Mar 2026) puts cumulative Damac payments across disclosures at 'at least $13 million, and possibly as much as $19 million'. The 2025 figures are not estimates: the filing gives each fee as an exact amount, and only asset values are ranges. Read line by line, the 2026 OGE filing shows DT Marks Abu Dhabi LLC $5,000,000 (licensee DAMAC Sky View Real Estate LLC), DT Marks Al Raha Beach LLC $5,000,000 (licensee DAMAC Properties Investment LLC), DT Marks Dubai LLC $1,335,140 (licence fee, Damac Crescent Properties LLC) and DT Dubai Golf Manager LLC $1,254,744 (management fee, Damac Crescent Properties LLC). That totals $12,589,884. CNBC's $11.3M matches the three licence fees without the management fee ($11,335,140). The cumulative Forbes and CREW figures remain estimates.

sub_claims.statement: The $20B data-centre pledge has turned into land in Ohio and New Jersey and a planned site in Kansas; nothing is reported as operating.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented for the pledge, the Davos update and the Canton and Edgerton sites. The New Jersey site is single-source on details. On 7 Jan 2025 Sajwani pledged at least $20B through Edgnex (now branded DAMAC Digital) for about 2GW across eight states (TX, AZ, OK, LA, OH, IL, MI, IN). He said 60-70% would be bank or bond debt. At Davos in Jan 2026 he said Damac had secured land and power worth about $12B, roughly 1GW, with land bought in Ohio and New Jersey and Texas under review. New Jersey is not on the original eight-state list. Ohio: county property records cited by CREW and trackers show DAMAC Digital Solution Ohio paid $36.5M in Dec 2025 for about 94 acres in south-east Canton (Stark County), bought from an Active Infrastructure-linked LLC (AIDC Canton 2). The 'Canton Orchard View' / Midwest Digital Gateway campus is on AEP Ohio's network and is planned for 2028, with phases to 2033. Canton annexed the land in late 2025. No megawatt figure has been published. Kansas: DAMAC Digital Solutions plans an $860M conversion of a nearly 400,000 sq ft warehouse at Logistics Park Kansas City in Edgerton. Edgerton is not on the original list either. Nothing operating in the US was found as of Nov 2026, and the 2-4 year build-out Sajwani gave runs to 2028-2030.

sub_claims.statement: Federal permitting or energy decisions have benefited Damac's sites.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented for the general policies. Any Damac-specific federal benefit is not found. On 10 Dec 2024 Trump posted that anyone investing $1B or more would get 'fully expedited approvals and permits, including, but not limited to, all Environmental approvals'. On 7 Jan 2025 he suggested expedited reviews for Sajwani's projects. EO 14318 (23 Jul 2025) defines qualifying data-centre projects by a commitment of $500M or more in capex, or more than 100MW of new load, among other tests. Such projects can get FAST-41 coverage and Commerce financial support. Edgerton ($860M) and probably the Canton campus would meet the dollar test. That is our inference: no source says either site has applied for or received FAST-41 coverage, federal financing, a DOE or FERC decision, or any other federal action. The approvals actually documented are local. Edgerton's planning commission denied the site plan 3-2 in June 2026. On 16 Jul 2026 the city council unanimously overrode that denial at a special meeting with no public comment. In Aug 2026 the city sued residents to void a citizen petition to ban hyperscale data centres. Canton handled the annexation and water service; its water superintendent estimated $3.7M to extend service to the site. Edgerton's project page says Damac sought no tax abatements. CNBC found no evidence that Damac's payments influenced federal policy.

sub_claims.statement: DT Marks Al Raha Beach LLC was formed the same day as the data-centre permitting order.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: single-source (CREW), carried over unchanged from C82. This check found no second source and could not reach the Delaware register. The EO date (23 Jul 2025) is documented. The formation-date match is CREW's observation and shows proximity, not causation.

sub_claims.statement: The Trump-Sajwani relationship goes back more than a decade and kept going through the transition and into the presidency.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (multiple outlets, Damac's own release, and a White House pool report). Timeline: Damac and the Trump Organization signed the Dubai golf deal (Damac Hills) around 2013; The National dates their acquaintance to 2011. In Dec 2016 Sajwani met Trump at Trump Tower. At NYE 2016 at Mar-a-Lago, Trump praised Sajwani's family on stage as 'the most beautiful people in Dubai'. On 11 Jan 2017 Trump said he had turned down a $2B Dubai deal from Sajwani. Damac confirmed talks worth about AED 7.3bn but did not confirm the $2B figure. In Feb 2017 Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr. opened the Trump International Golf Club Dubai. In 2018 Eric and Don Jr. attended the wedding of Sajwani's daughter in Dubai. On 20 Nov 2024 Sajwani told Bloomberg he was 'open for new Trump projects'. On 31 Dec 2024 Sajwani posted a photo with Trump and Elon Musk from the Mar-a-Lago New Year's party; this is single-source, from Raw Story's write-up of his posts. On 7 Jan 2025 came the Mar-a-Lago data-centre announcement. On 22 Apr 2025 Sajwani posted that he had met Trump in the Oval Office 'once again' and had breakfast at the White House with Musk and Shivon Zilis. On 23 Apr 2025 Damac issued a Business Wire statement looking forward to Trump's Gulf visit. On 16 May 2025 the White House pool report lists Sajwani among business attendees at the US-UAE forum at Qasr Al Watan. In 2025 the two new Abu Dhabi licences followed. Proximity to the president is documented. No source documents any specific request made at these meetings. Hope Hicks said in Jan 2017 that the two did not discuss business at the 2016 party.

sub_claims.statement: Sajwani or Damac has dealings with Trump family crypto ventures (WLF, USD1, $TRUMP).
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: not found. Searches turned up no Sajwani or Damac investment in WLF, the WLFI token, USD1, $TRUMP or American Bitcoin, and no seat at the $TRUMP dinner. Damac's documented crypto activity is unrelated to the Trumps. On 9 Jan 2025, two days after the Mar-a-Lago announcement, Damac signed a $1B real-world-asset tokenisation deal with MANTRA, fronted by Amira Sajwani. MANTRA's OM token then fell more than 90% on 13 Apr 2025; the team blamed exchange liquidations. No Trump link to MANTRA was found. Some outlets (Benzinga/Cryptonews) say the crypto-accepting Trump Tower Dubai is a Damac project. It is a Dar Global project (C31), so this is a misattribution.

sub_claims.statement: Damac and Sajwani's public statements about the Trump ties and the 2025-26 payments.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented. Damac did not respond to CNBC about the 2025 fees, and this check found no Damac comment on CREW's Abu Dhabi or Ohio reports. Sajwani's public line has been promotional. In Nov 2024 he said he was open to new Trump projects. In Jan 2025 he called the US expansion a milestone and qualified the $20B as dependent on 'the opportunity, the market'. His 2025 posts and releases praised the Oval Office meeting and Trump's Gulf trip. In Jan 2017 Damac confirmed the declined offer. The White House says the president's assets are in a trust managed by his children and that there are no conflicts (C70).

sub_claims.statement: CREW links Damac's Ohio project to rising Ohio utility prices.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented that CREW makes the claim (12 Mar 2026). CREW sets Damac's $36.5M Canton purchase beside a Feb 2026 Canton city utility-rate rise driven partly by electricity costs. Damac's Canton campus is not built and is planned for 2028, so it cannot have caused 2025-26 price rises. FactCheck.org (Oct 2026) says data centres contributed to Ohio's capacity-market increases (one estimate: about $16 a month, 63% of it attributed to data centres), but the cause is broader. The headline juxtaposition is CREW's framing, not evidence that Damac affected prices.

corrections: The claim implies federal permitting or energy decisions benefited Damac's sites; none was found. The documented approvals are local (Edgerton council override, 16 Jul 2026; Canton annexation and water).
The claim lists 'New Year's Eve at Mar-a-Lago' as one event; the documented on-stage praise is NYE 2016. NYE 2024 attendance rests on Sajwani's own posts as relayed by Raw Story.
Some crypto outlets call the crypto-accepting Trump Tower Dubai a Damac project; it is Dar Global's.
Damac's US footprint (New Jersey; Edgerton, Kansas) includes states that were not among the eight announced on 7 Jan 2025.
One syndicated AP summary renders a disclosure figure as Sajwani 'contributing' $1-5M to Trump's 2016 campaign. That looks garbled (foreign nationals cannot donate), and it is not used here.

16 Nov 2026: Claimed: the 2025 Damac total (about $11.3-12.5M) is an estimate, and which subsidiary paid which Abu Dhabi entity is not specified. The record shows: the 2026 OGE filing lists four exact Damac-linked fee lines totalling $12,589,884, and names DAMAC Sky View Real Estate LLC as licensee of DT Marks Abu Dhabi LLC and DAMAC Properties Investment LLC as licensee of DT Marks Al Raha Beach LLC. The two payer-to-entity relationships have been corrected to match.
denials_and_context: Damac did not respond to CNBC (Aug 2026) and has not publicly addressed CREW's reports.
CNBC found no evidence that Damac's payments influenced the July 2025 permitting order; the order is general policy covering any large data-centre sponsor.
Hope Hicks (Jan 2017) said Trump and Sajwani did not discuss business at the 2016 New Year's party; Trump said he declined Damac's 2017 offer to avoid conflicts.
The White House says there are no conflicts of interest and that Trump's businesses are run by his children.
Sajwani conditioned the $20B on market conditions and bank financing. Analysts (E&E News, Jan 2025; Bloomberg via Fortune) questioned grid capacity and his ability to fund it.
Background: an Egyptian court convicted Sajwani in absentia in 2011 over a land deal; he called it politically motivated (BuzzFeed, 2017). This is not tied to any Trump decision.

leads.title: Edgerton, Kansas: city sues residents to stop a data-centre ban covering Damac's site
leads.why_connected: A Trump business partner's $860M project was approved by a council override with no public comment, then the city sued petitioners. Who brokered Logistics Park Kansas City (NorthPoint) and any state incentives are unexamined.

leads.title: Damac's Canton, Ohio campus: PJM/AEP Ohio interconnection and power arrangements
leads.why_connected: The Canton site's power supply (AEP Ohio data-centre tariff, PJM queue, any behind-the-meter generation) would show whether any federal or FERC-jurisdictional decision touches a Trump partner's project.

leads.title: Damac's New Jersey data-centre land
leads.why_connected: Sajwani said at Davos that land was bought in New Jersey, a state not in the original pledge. Location, price and seller are unreported.

leads.title: DAMAC Digital's 6,000MW global landbank and financing
leads.why_connected: Sajwani said 60-70% of the US build would be debt-financed. Lenders and any US government-backed financing (EO 14318 allows Commerce loans) are unknown.

changes: Abu Dhabi fees: upheld ($5M per entity, CREW from Trump's OGE disclosure). CREW's own wording is that the entities 'appear to be related to unannounced developments in Abu Dhabi'; the summary now carries that qualifier. Fresh searches (Gulf News, The National Sept 2026 overview) found no Damac or Trump Organization Abu Dhabi launch through Nov 2026; Trump-branded Gulf launches found are Dar Global's.

US sites: upheld. Trackers and CREW confirm DAMAC Digital Solution Ohio bought ~94 acres in SE Canton in Dec 2025; Ingram's and DCD confirm the $860M Edgerton conversion, the 3-2 planning-commission denial and the later go-ahead. Nothing operating.
Federal approvals: none found; upheld as unverified. DT Marks Al Raha Beach's same-day formation remains single-source (CREW) and its relationship label now says so.

16 Nov 2026: replaced the '$11.3-12.5M estimate' with the exact $12,589,884 from four filing lines; explained CNBC's $11.3M as the licence fees without the $1,254,744 management fee; swapped the two Abu Dhabi payer-to-entity relationships to match the licensees named in the filing (Sky View pays DT Marks Abu Dhabi; Properties Investment pays DT Marks Al Raha Beach).
